summary: Petition under Section 79 and Section 142 of the Electricity Act 2003 read with Regulation 12 “Power to Remove Difficulty” of Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Deviation Settlement Mechanism and related matters) Regulations, 2024, read with Regulation 111 of Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 1999 dealing with persistent default in payment of Deviation charges applicable under the CERC (Deviation Settlement Mechanism and related matters) Regulations 2024 and other associated issues. 3. The Petitioner, Northern Regional Load Despatch Centre (NRLDC) filed the present petition under Section 79 and Section 142 of the Electricity Act 2003 read with Regulation 12 “Power to Remove Difficulty” of Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Deviation Settlement Mechanism and related matters) Regulations, 2024, read with Regulation 111 of Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 1999 dealing with persistent default in payment of Deviation charges as well as regarding the payment of Net Deviation & Ancillary Services Pool Account, Deficit Recovery for the period before 16.09.2024 (Statement of Legacy Dues), applicable under the CERC (Deviation Settlement Mechanism and related matters) Regulations 2024 and other associated matters. The Petitioner seeks intervention from the Commission regarding difficulties faced in discharging its statutory functions under the DSM Regulations, 2024, particularly in relation to the persistent default by JKPCL in paying deviation charges. - (g) _Issue any or such further order or orders as may be deemed just and proper in the facts and circumstances of this case._ - (h) In Petition No. 28/MP/2022, the Commission, vide its order dated 13.01.2024, made specific observations regarding instances of wilful default or delay in the timely payment of deviation charges. The Commission directed the Petitioner to actively monitor such instances in the future and report them to the Commission for appropriate penal action under Section 142 of the Electricity Act, 2003. - (o) In view of the above issues, the Petitioner requested the Commission to issue appropriate orders under Section 142 of the Electricity Act, read with Regulation 111 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 1999 and Regulation 12 (Power to issue directions) of the DSM Regulations 2024. 6. During the course of the hearing, the counsel for the Petitioner made oral submissions in support of the prayers in the petition. After hearing the counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission admitted the Petition and directed the Respondents to file their reply and the Petitioner to file the rejoinder, if any. 7. During the course of the hearing, the counsel for the Petitioner pointed out that the Respondent, J&K SLDC, did not file its reply in the matter. Further, no one appeared on behalf of the Respondents, despite notice. Accordingly, the Commission, as a last opportunity, permitted the Respondents to file their replies and the Petitioner to file its rejoinder, if any. ## **Submissions of the Respondent No. 2, JKPCL, dated 30.09.2025, in compliance with the Record of Proceedings (ROP) of the hearing dated 26.08.2025** - (c) The matter regarding the opening of the Letter of Credit in favour of various CPSUs, Gencos, etc., was taken up with the higher authorities. As and when the necessary approvals/ instructions in this regard are received, the same would be complied with. - (e) The Petitioner requested that the Commission exercise its discretion in favour of the Respondent JKPCL and not pass orders under Section 142 of the Act. 9. During the course of the hearing, the counsel for the Petitioner reiterated that there was a persistent default by the Respondents in the payment of the deviation charges, including the legacy dues, under the DSM Regulations and hence the present petition was filed. In response, counsel for the Respondent pointed out that a lump-sum amount of Rs. 30 crore was paid to the Petitioner towards deviation charges, but, due to financial constraints, the Respondent may be granted a six-month extension of time to clear the balance dues. Accordingly, the Commission directed the Petitioner to respond to the Respondent's specific prayer for a six-month extension of time for payment of the balance dues in the rejoinder affidavit. ## **Rejoinder by the Petitioner on 20.11.2025 in compliance with the ROP of the hearing dated 27.10.2025** 11. During the course of the hearing, the counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner has filed a rejoinder affidavit, elaborating on the conditions for the Respondent’s payment of dues. In response, the learned counsel for the Respondent, JKPCL, while objecting to the proposal of NRLDC for the monthly payment of the dues, submitted that, on account of the financial constraints, it may be granted six months’ time to clear the dues. The Commission, after hearing the parties, reserved its order in the petition. 12. The Commission has heard the learned counsels for the Petitioner and the Respondents and has carefully perused the records. 19. The Commission observes the submission of the Petitioner seeking to empower RLDCs to initiate regulatory measures (regulate entirely access, including any previously approved access, for the sale and purchase of electricity through short-term contracts or power exchange) to deal with persistent default in payment of regulatory charges, viz. Deviation charge including interest, Reactive Energy charge, Congestion charge, the amount payable under all kinds of ancillary services (including TRAS & SRAS and opening and maintaining of Letter of Credit (LC), etc.) The Commission also takes note of the Respondent's submission that any such powers can be granted to RLDCs only by amendment to the appropriate regulations or by the notification of new regulations.
